children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.checks
children.doc:
Consistency checks of one antenna result, as :class:`pinneapple_analysis.trust.Check` / ``TrustReport``.

Each check is a relation the numbers must satisfy whatever solver produced them (IEEE Std 145 definitions):

=============================  ===========================================================  ========
check                          relation                                                     critical
=============================  ===========================================================  ========
``realized_gain``              ``G_realized = G_IEEE + 10 log10(1 - |S11|^2)``                no
``efficiency_is_G_over_D``     ``e_rad = G / D`` (``10 log10 e = G_dBi - D_dBi``)             no
``efficiency_le_1``            ``e_rad <= 1`` (a passive antenna cannot radiate more than    yes
                               it accepts)
``peak_ge_boresight``          the pattern peak is not below the boresight value             no
``directivity_le_hw``          ``D <= 7.28 L / lambda`` (+ 0.5 dB), :mod:`.bounds`           no
``s11_resolved``               an S11 interpolated by a rational (vector) fit is only        no
                               trusted with enough solved frequencies in the band
``power_closure``              radiated power from the far-field pattern = Poynting flux     no
                               through the radiation surface (within 10 %): the mesh
                               resolves the fields the far field is computed from
=============================  ===========================================================  ========

A check whose inputs are missing (``None`` / NaN) is ``not_run`` with the reason; it never passes silently.

functions.name: check_realized_gain
functions.sig: (g_dbi, g_real_dbi, s11_db, *, tol_db: float = 0.1) -> Check
functions.doc: ``G_realized = G + 10 log10(1 - |S11|^2)`` within ``tol_db``.

functions.name: check_efficiency_ratio
functions.sig: (g_dbi, d_dbi, eff, *, tol_db: float = 0.1) -> Check
functions.doc: ``e_rad = G / D`` within ``tol_db``.

functions.name: check_efficiency_le_one
functions.sig: (eff, *, tol: float = 0.01) -> Check
functions.doc: Radiation efficiency at most 1 (+ ``tol`` for the far-field quadrature). Critical.

functions.name: check_peak_ge_boresight
functions.sig: (peak_dbi, bore_dbi, *, tol_db: float = 0.05) -> Check

functions.name: check_directivity_limit
functions.sig: (d_dbi, length_m, f_hz, *, margin_db: float = 0.5, kind: str = 'hw') -> Check
functions.doc: Directivity below the end-fire limit of :mod:`.bounds` for a length ``length_m`` (+ ``margin_db``).

functions.name: check_s11_resolved
functions.sig: (n_solved: int | None, *, interpolated: bool, min_points: int = 5) -> Check
functions.doc:
An S11 from a rational (vector-fit) interpolation needs at least ``min_points`` solved frequencies.

With fewer, the fit has as many poles as data and its values between the samples are not evidence.

functions.name: check_power_closure
functions.sig: (p_pattern, p_surface, *, rtol: float = 0.1) -> Check
functions.doc: Far-field power (integral of the pattern) against the near-field Poynting flux through the same surface.

functions.name: antenna_checks
functions.sig: (row: Mapping[str, Any], *, length_m: float | None = None, n_solved: int | None = None, interpolated: bool = False, min_points: int = 5, tol_db: float = 0.1, margin_db: float = 0.5, model: str = '') -> TrustReport
functions.doc:
Every check above on one table row (the columns of :mod:`.runner`).

``length_m``: the antenna length for the directivity limit (default: ``row["Lb"]`` in mm).

children.summary: Consistency checks of one antenna result, as pinneapple_analysis.trust.Check / TrustReport.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.design
children.doc:
Design loop of a printed end-fire antenna: DOE, multi-objective optimisation, active learning with solver
verification, multi-fidelity bias correction and a trust card per prediction.

* :func:`doe` -- Latin hypercube or Sobol samples of :data:`AVA_RANGES` (configurable), mapped by
  :func:`ava_transform` (director and slots switched on/off, the director placed as a fraction of the length) and
  filtered by :func:`.ava.layout` (unbuildable designs are skipped and counted);
* :func:`optimize` -- NSGA-II (:mod:`pinneapple_design.design_optimizer.methods`) on surrogates: maximise the
  minimum realized gain over the band, minimise the board area, subject to ``max S11 <= -10 dB`` over the band;
* :func:`active_learning` -- rounds of: fit the GP, pick candidates by predictive variance
  (:class:`pinneapple_data.active_learning.VarianceBasedAL`), simulate them, record the error of the prediction made
  *before* the simulation (prospective error, never in-sample), add them;
* :func:`multi_fidelity` -- coarse simulations (``res`` 0.25 wavelength) for many designs, fine ones (``res`` 0.2)
  for a few: the coarse-to-fine bias per frequency is learnt on the fine designs and validated leaving one fine
  design out;
* :func:`prediction_card` -- a :class:`~pinneapple_analysis.trust.TrustReport` for one surrogate prediction: inside
  the training domain, geometry buildable, uncertainty below a threshold, below the physical limit, surrogate
  out-of-sample error known.

functions.name: ava_transform
functions.sig: (sample: Mapping[str, float], *, fixed: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
A raw sample of :data:`AVA_RANGES` to AVA parameters: ``dir_x`` from a fraction of ``Lb`` to mm, director off
when ``dir_a < 4`` mm, slot fields ignored when ``nslot = 0``; ``fixed`` overrides (e.g. ``res``).

functions.name: is_buildable
functions.sig: (params: Mapping[str, Any]) -> bool

functions.name: training_box
functions.sig: (designs: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], keys: Sequence[str] = ('Lb', 'W', 'Wa'), ranges: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None) -> dict[str, tuple[float, float]]
functions.doc: ``ranges`` with ``keys`` narrowed to the span of ``designs``: optimise where the surrogate was trained.

functions.name: doe
functions.sig: (n: int, ranges: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None, *, method: str = 'lhs', seed: int = 0, transform: Callable[[Mapping[str, float]], dict[str, Any]] | None = ava_transform, valid: Callable[[Mapping[str, Any]], bool] | None = is_buildable, max_factor: int = 30) -> tuple[list[dict[str, Any]], dict[str, int]]
functions.doc:
``n`` valid designs from a space-filling sample; returns ``(designs, {"drawn": .., "invalid": ..})``.

Draws in batches (``pinneapple_data.parameter_sampling.sample_parameters``) until ``n`` designs pass ``valid``
or ``max_factor * n`` have been drawn.

functions.name: band_metrics
functions.sig: (models: Mapping[str, _Model], params: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], freqs: Sequence[float], *, gain: str = 'Greal_bore_dBi', s11: str = 'S11_dB') -> dict[str, np.ndarray]
functions.doc: Predicted minimum gain, its std at the arg-min, and maximum S11 over ``freqs`` for each design.

functions.name: optimize
functions.sig: (models: Mapping[str, _Model], freqs: Sequence[float], *, ranges: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None, fixed: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, budget: int = 600, seed: int = 0, method: str = 'nsga2', s11_max: float = -10.0, gain: str = 'Greal_bore_dBi', s11: str = 'S11_dB') -> OptimizationOutcome
functions.doc:
Multi-objective search on the surrogates ``models[gain]`` and ``models[s11]`` (fit beforehand).

Objectives: maximise the minimum predicted gain over ``freqs``, minimise ``Lb * W``; constraint: the maximum
predicted S11 over ``freqs`` at most ``s11_max``. Unbuildable designs are marked invalid (never on the front).

functions.name: active_learning
functions.sig: (simulate: Callable[[list[dict[str, Any]], int], ResultTable], table: ResultTable, freqs: Sequence[float], *, target: str = 'Greal_bore_dBi', rounds: int = 2, per_round: int = 2, ranges: Mapping[str, tuple[float, float]] | None = None, fixed: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, n_candidates: int = 400, seed: int = 0, model: Callable[[], _Model] = GPModel) -> tuple[ResultTable, list[ALRound]]
functions.doc:
Variance-driven active learning with verification by the simulator.

``simulate(designs, round) -> ResultTable`` runs the solver (e.g. :class:`.runner.CLISimulator`). Each round
fits ``model`` on ``table``, selects ``per_round`` buildable candidates with
:class:`pinneapple_data.active_learning.VarianceBasedAL` (probability proportional to the mean predictive
variance over ``freqs``), predicts them, simulates them, records the prospective error and appends them.

functions.name: multi_fidelity
functions.sig: (coarse: ResultTable, fine: ResultTable, target: str) -> dict[str, Any]
functions.doc:
Coarse-to-fine bias of ``target`` per frequency, validated leaving one fine design out.

Pairs (tag, f) present in both tables; returns the mean bias per frequency (fine - coarse), the RMSE of the
raw coarse values against the fine ones, and the RMSE of coarse + bias learnt without the held-out design.

functions.name: prediction_card
functions.sig: (model: _Model, params: Mapping[str, Any], f_ghz: float, train: ResultTable, *, target: str = 'Greal_bore_dBi', std_max_db: float = 1.0, lodo_rmse: float | None = None, rmse_max_db: float = 1.5, margin_db: float = 0.5) -> TrustReport
functions.doc:
Trust card of one surrogate prediction (mean, std in ``details``).

Checks: ``in_domain`` (every physical feature of :func:`.surrogates.physical_features` inside the range of the
training rows; critical), ``buildable``
(critical), ``uncertainty`` (std <= ``std_max_db``), ``below_physical_limit`` (gain or directivity below the
Hansen-Woodyard limit + ``margin_db``), ``surrogate_error_known`` (out-of-sample RMSE given and below
``rmse_max_db``).

children.summary: Design loop of a printed end-fire antenna: DOE, multi-objective optimisation, active learning with solver verification, multi-fidelity bias correction and a trust card per prediction.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.package
children.doc:
Read an external study package from a local folder and re-run one of its designs.

A package is a folder with a results table (one row per (design, frequency), the columns of :mod:`.runner`) and,
optionally, the parametric command-line script that produced it. Nothing from it is copied into the repository:
it is read where it is. An optional ``package.json`` says which files to use and how to call the script::

    {"table": "results.csv",
     "script": "ava_cli.py",
     "argv": ["{python}", "{script}"],           # the command before the design / frequency flags
     "flags": {"params": "--params", "freq": "--freq", "out": "--out", "tag": "--tag"},
     "length_col": "Lb"}

Without it the first ``*.csv`` / ``*.tsv`` / ``*.txt`` table and the first ``*.py`` script are used with the flags of
:mod:`.ava` (``--params JSON --freq GHz --out DIR --tag TAG``, ``result.json`` in the output folder).

methods.doc: A :class:`.runner.CLISimulator` on the package's script (one frequency per process).

functions.doc: The package in folder ``root`` (see the module docstring).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.runner
children.doc:
Drive an external parametric simulator script, one process per sample (and per frequency), and read its tables.

:class:`CLISimulator` runs any command-line script that takes a design and frequencies and writes its result
(``result.json`` with ``{"status": "ok" | "invalid", "rows": [...]}`` by default, or anything a ``parse`` callable
reads). Each call is a separate process with a timeout, so a crash, a memory blow-up or a hung solve costs one sample,
not the study. Lessons measured while running EMerge on a 4-core, 15 GB machine, built in as defaults:

* EMerge's PARDISO backend can die with SIGBUS when MKL is not usable: on SIGBUS the sample is retried once with
  ``fallback_args`` (for :mod:`.ava` the default is already SuperLU; ``--pardiso`` opts in);
* three frequencies in one process with SuperLU went past 15 GB and were SIGKILLed: ``per_frequency=True`` runs one
  frequency per process (each frequency also gets its own mesh sized to its wavelength);
* ``grid.model_S`` (the rational S-parameter model) fails with a single frequency: :mod:`.ava` reads ``grid.S``.

Every run records its exit status, wall time and peak memory (``ru_maxrss`` of that child, from ``os.wait4``).

The table format, one row per (design, frequency): ``tag``, the design parameters, ``f_GHz``, ``S11_dB``,
``D_bore_dBi``, ``G_bore_dBi``, ``Greal_bore_dBi``, ``D_peak_dBi``, ``Greal_peak_dBi``, ``rad_eff`` (extra columns
are kept). :func:`read_table` reads it from CSV, TSV or whitespace-separated text; :func:`write_table` writes CSV.

classes.sig: (argv: Sequence[str], workdir: str, *, per_frequency: bool = True, timeout: float = 3600.0, params_flag: str = '--params', freq_flag: str = '--freq', out_flag: str = '--out', tag_flag: str | None = '--tag', fallback_args: Sequence[str] = (), parse: Callable[[str], tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]], str]] | None = None, env: Mapping[str, str] | None = None, log: Callable[[str], None] | None = None...

Run ``argv + [params_flag, json, freq_flag, f..., out_flag, dir, tag_flag, tag]`` per design.

``argv``: the command (e.g. ``[sys.executable, "script.py"]``); ``per_frequency``: one process per frequency;
``timeout``: seconds per process; ``fallback_args``: appended for one retry after a SIGBUS; ``parse(out_dir)``
returns ``(status, rows, message)``; ``env``: extra environment variables (thread counts, log levels);
``extra_args``: arguments added to every command (e.g. ``["--scan", "0", "30"]``); ``resume``: reuse the
``result.json`` an earlier (interrupted) run left in the same folder when its status is ``ok`` and the
parameters it was run with (``runner_params.json``, written by the runner) match, instead of solving again
(recorded with ``message="reused"``).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.scene3d
children.doc:
3-D views of an antipodal Vivaldi from its solved fields, on the generic studio scene of PINNeAPPle.

Everything is built on :mod:`pinneapple_tools.visualization.studio` (``Scene`` / ``Surface`` / ``Animation``, glTF
and USD export, the three.js viewer, Blender Cycles with the jet colour bar); nothing here draws pixels itself.

* :func:`antenna_surfaces` -- the substrate (translucent laminate) and the copper of both faces (flares, slots,
  director, feed line) of :func:`.ava.layout`, 35 um thick, in millimetres, end-fire along +y;
* :func:`read_farfield` / :func:`balloon` -- the far field ``ff_<f>GHz.npz`` saved by :mod:`.ava` as a radiation
  balloon centred on the board: radius ``R * (G - floor) / (G_max - floor)``, coloured by the gain in dBi
  (``G = 4 pi U / P_acc``); the directivity of every vertex is kept too (``D = 4 pi U / P_rad``), so the balloon's
  maximum is the table's ``D_peak_dBi`` by construction (:func:`farfield_metrics` checks it);
* :func:`read_nearfield` -- the complex E on the two cut planes ``nf_<f>GHz.npz`` (substrate mid-plane and the
  vertical plane through the end-fire axis), as coloured surfaces: ``|E|`` in dB below the plane's 99.5th
  percentile (the singular feed gap would set the scale otherwise; clipped at 0 dB), or the instantaneous
  ``Re(E_x e^{j wt})`` over the same percentile of ``|E_x|`` (clipped to +-1);
* :func:`frequency_scene` -- antenna + balloon + cuts over the solved frequencies (one frame per frequency, stepped,
  never blended): the balloon changes shape with :meth:`Animation.add_surface_shape`;
* :func:`phase_scene` -- the cuts over one period (wt from 0 to 360 degrees) at one frequency;
* :func:`build_3d` -- every file: glTF and USD per frequency, the self-contained viewers, Blender stills (beauty and
  balloon) and the GIF / MP4 of the sweep and of the phase.

End-to-end studies of a printed end-fire antenna, as library calls (the example and the Flow Studio call these).

* :func:`limits_report` -- the end-fire lengths a target gain needs across a band and the feasibility frequency of
  given lengths (no solver);
* :func:`open_study` -- the open AVA model of :mod:`.ava` in EMerge: DOE, coarse and fine runs (one frequency per
  process), checks of every row, multi-fidelity bias, LODO of four surrogates, NSGA-II on the GP, verification of
  the best predicted design, active learning, figures, ``summary.json`` and CSV tables;
* :func:`render_3d` -- named designs re-solved with their near field, then every 3-D output of :mod:`.scene3d`
  (glTF / USD per frequency, self-contained viewers, Blender stills and GIF / MP4) and the balloon-against-table
  consistency;
* :func:`package_study` -- an external package (results table + CLI script, :mod:`.package`): checks, limits, LODO,
  figures, and a re-run of one of its designs compared with the table.

Each returns a JSON-able summary of measured values only.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.antenna.surrogates
children.doc:
Surrogates of an antenna quantity over (design, frequency), and honest validation of them.

Models (all ``fit(table, target)`` / ``predict(params_list, f_ghz) -> (mean, std)``):

* :class:`FrequencyMean` -- the mean of the target over the training designs at each frequency (interpolated in
  frequency): the baseline any model must beat;
* :class:`HWOffset` -- the Hansen-Woodyard limit ``10 log10(7.28 L / lambda)`` plus one fitted offset (one
  parameter: physics carries the length and frequency dependence);
* :class:`LinearPhysics` -- ridge regression on physical features (:func:`physical_features`: ``log(L/lambda)``,
  ``W/lambda``, ``Wa/lambda``, slots on/off, director on/off);
* :class:`GPModel` -- Gaussian process (squared-exponential, one length scale per feature, hyper-parameters by
  maximum marginal likelihood) on the same features plus the HW limit as its mean; returns a predictive std.

Validation: :func:`lodo` (leave one *design* out: every frequency of the held-out design leaves together, so the
model never sees the design it predicts) and :func:`holdout` (a fixed set of test designs). Leaving one row out
would leak the design through its other frequencies and flatter the model.

classes.name: FrequencyMean
classes.doc: Mean of the training targets at each frequency (linear interpolation between frequencies).

classes.name: HWOffset
classes.doc: Hansen-Woodyard limit plus one fitted offset (dB).

classes.name: LinearPhysics
classes.sig: (ridge: float = 0.001)
classes.doc: Ridge regression on :func:`physical_features` (standardised; constant features dropped).

classes.name: GPModel
classes.sig: (prior: str = 'hw', restarts: int = 4, seed: int = 0, features = None)
classes.doc:
GP on :func:`physical_features` with the HW limit as prior mean (``prior="hw"``) or a constant.

Squared-exponential kernel with one length scale per feature, signal and noise variances; hyper-parameters by
maximum log marginal likelihood (L-BFGS-B from a few starts). ``predict`` returns the mean and the predictive
std including the fitted noise. ``features(params, f_ghz) -> (n, d)`` replaces :func:`physical_features` for
any other design space (then use ``prior="const"``), e.g. ``columns("feed_gain_dBi", "side")``.

classes.name: ValidationResult
classes.doc: Out-of-sample predictions of each model; ``rmse[model]`` in the target's unit.

methods.doc: Fraction of held-out values inside mean +- 1.96 std (calibration of the stated uncertainty).

functions.doc:
``(n, 5)`` features of each (design, frequency): ``log(L/lambda)``, ``W/lambda``, ``Wa/lambda``,
``nslot > 0`` and ``dir_a > 0``. Lengths in mm (``Lb``, ``W``, ``Wa``).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.constants
children.doc:
Physical constants of electromagnetics, SI, CODATA 2022 (NIST, https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/).

Since the 2019 SI redefinition ``c``, ``e``, ``h`` and ``k_B`` are exact and ``mu0`` is measured
(``mu0 = 4 pi alpha hbar / (e^2 c)``); ``eps0 = 1 / (mu0 c^2)`` follows from it. ``mu0`` differs from the
pre-2019 value ``4 pi 1e-7`` by about 5e-10 relative, far below any discretisation error in this package.
children.summary: Physical constants of electromagnetics, SI, CODATA 2022 (NIST, https://physics.nist.gov/cuu/Constants/).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.eddy
children.doc:
Time-harmonic 2D eddy currents in A_z with solid conductors (linear media).

Phasors with ``exp(+j omega t)``. In a solid conductor ``c`` the current density is
``J = sigma (-j omega A + u_c)`` where ``u_c`` is the (uniform) voltage per metre along z, an extra
unknown fixed by the net current ``int_c J dS = I_c`` (``I_c = 0`` for an insulated piece such as a
magnet segment). The system::

    int nu grad A . grad v + j omega int sigma A v - sum_c u_c int_c sigma v = int J_s v
    -j omega int_c sigma A + u_c int_c sigma                                 = I_c

is assembled with P1 elements (consistent mass matrix) and solved with a sparse direct solver.
Losses are ``int |J|^2 / (2 sigma)`` (time average, peak phasors).

functions.name: solve_time_harmonic
functions.sig: (mesh: Mesh2D, nu: np.ndarray, sigma: np.ndarray, omega: float, conductors: Sequence[np.ndarray], currents: Sequence[complex], J_source: np.ndarray | None = None, dirichlet: np.ndarray | None = None, dirichlet_values = None) -> TimeHarmonicSolution
functions.doc:
Solve for A (complex). ``conductors``: element masks of solid conductors; ``currents``: their
net current phasors (A). ``sigma`` (M,) is used inside conductors only.

children.summary: Time-harmonic 2D eddy currents in A_z with solid conductors (linear media).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.electrostatics
children.doc:
2-D electrostatics on P1 triangles: ``-div(eps grad phi) = rho`` with electrodes at fixed potentials.

It is the operator of :func:`.fem.solve_magnetostatic` with ``nu -> eps`` and ``J -> rho`` (the two problems are
the same Poisson equation with a piecewise-constant coefficient), so it inherits that solver's assembly and
constraints. Per unit length along z: the energy is ``W = (1/2) int eps |grad phi|^2 dA`` and the capacitance
between an electrode at ``V`` and grounded ones is ``C = 2 W / V^2`` (F/m), which converges at twice the order of
the potential's H1 error (second order on P1 for smooth fields).

Planar (``x, y``) geometry only; axisymmetric electrostatics would need the ``r`` weight.

functions.name: solve_electrostatic
functions.sig: (mesh: Mesh2D, eps_r, electrodes: Mapping[str, tuple[np.ndarray, float]] | None = None, rho = None, dirichlet = None, dirichlet_values = None) -> ElectrostaticSolution
functions.doc:
Potential for element relative permittivities ``eps_r`` (scalar or (M,)), charge density ``rho``
(C/m^3 per element) and electrodes ``{name: (node indices, potential)}`` (or raw ``dirichlet`` nodes and
values). Nodes in no electrode carry the natural condition ``D.n = 0`` (a symmetry plane or an open side).

functions.name: capacitance
functions.sig: (sol: ElectrostaticSolution, V: float) -> float
functions.doc:
``C = 2 W / V^2`` (F/m) for one electrode at ``V`` and the others grounded, no free charge.

Returns
-------
C : float [F/m]
    Capacitance per unit length.

children.summary: 2-D electrostatics on P1 triangles: -div(eps grad phi) = rho with electrodes at fixed potentials.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fdtd
children.doc:
Finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) solution of Maxwell's curl equations on the Yee grid, in 1-D, 2-D and 3-D.

One code path for all dimensions: the grid has ``(nx, ny, nz)`` nodes and an axis with one node is a direction of
invariance (``d/dz = 0`` in 2-D, where the six components hold the TMz set ``Ez, Hx, Hy`` and the TEz set
``Hz, Ex, Ey`` at once). Component positions follow Yee (1966): ``Ex`` at ``(i+1/2, j, k)``, ``Ey`` at
``(i, j+1/2, k)``, ``Ez`` at ``(i, j, k+1/2)``, ``Hx`` at ``(i, j+1/2, k+1/2)`` and so on; E at integer time steps,
H at half steps (leapfrog). References: A. Taflove and S. C. Hagness, *Computational Electrodynamics: The
Finite-Difference Time-Domain Method*, 3rd ed., Artech House, 2005 (TH below), ch. 3-4 (scheme, Courant limit,
numerical dispersion), ch. 5 (total-field / scattered-field), ch. 7 (CPML), ch. 9 (dispersive media).

* **Stability.** ``dt <= 1 / (c sqrt(sum 1/dx_i^2))`` (TH eq. 4.65); :class:`YeeGrid` refuses a larger step
  unless ``allow_unstable=True`` (used by the test that shows the blow-up).
* **Boundaries** per side: ``"pec"`` (tangential E = 0 on the outer node plane), ``"pmc"`` (tangential H = 0 half a
  cell outside it, by an odd image), ``"periodic"``, ``"bloch"`` (Floquet phase ``exp(-j k_b L)`` across the
  period; complex fields) and ``"cpml"``: the convolutional PML of Roden and Gedney (Microw. Opt. Technol. Lett. 27,
  2000; TH sec. 7.9) on the outer ``npml`` cells with polynomial grading of ``sigma`` and ``kappa`` and a linear
  ``alpha`` (TH eqs. 7.60, 7.79, 7.102), terminated by PEC.
* **Media.** Per-node ``eps_inf``, ``mu_r``, ``sigma``, magnetic ``sigma_m`` (an E component takes the harmonic mean
  of the permittivity of the two nodes it joins, the series rule for E normal to an interface between them, and the
  arithmetic mean of the conductivity; ``harmonic_eps=False`` uses the arithmetic mean), and dispersive poles (:mod:`.media`): Drude (polarisation
  current, trapezoidal ADE), Debye (polarisation, trapezoidal) and Lorentz (polarisation, central second order),
  each solved together with the E update (TH sec. 9.4-9.6).
* **Sources.** Soft or hard E sources, impressed currents ``J`` (a Hertzian dipole is one cell of ``J``), and a
  total-field / scattered-field box for an axis-aligned plane wave, driven by an auxiliary 1-D FDTD with the same
  ``dx`` and ``dt``, so the incident wave has the main grid's own numerical dispersion and leaks only at round-off.
* **Monitors.** Probes (time series), running DFTs of any component over any region (phasors with the
  ``exp(+j omega t)`` convention of this package, E and H stamped at their own times), Poynting flux through a plane
  from the DFTs, and the discrete electromagnetic energy.

:func:`numerical_dispersion` gives the exact dispersion relation of the scheme, :func:`courant_limit` the step
limit.

classes.name: YeeGrid
classes.doc:
Node counts ``shape = (nx, ny, nz)`` (use 1 for invariant axes), spacings and the time step (``courant`` is
the fraction of the stability limit).

methods.name: coords
methods.doc: Coordinates of the nodes of a component along x, y, z (half-cell offsets of the Yee cell).

classes.name: DFTMonitor

polarisations it reduces, but does not remove, the staircase error (Fa

``W = (1/2) sum eps E^{n-1} . E^n dV + (1/2) sum mu |H^{n-1/2}|^2 dV``. In a lossless cavity with PEC or PMC
walls the Yee scheme conserves this quantity exactly (to round-off) for any stable time step; before the
first step it is the plain energy of the initial fields.

methods.doc:
``(t, fields)``: all six components at the integer nodes at ``t = (n - 1/2) dt``, the time of the stored

offsets (second order in space and time). It is the input layout of
:func:`pinneapple_physics.maxwell_checks.maxwell_checks` (H components).

classes.name: NearToFarField
classes.sig: (sim: FDTD, freqs, box)
classes.doc:
Near-to-far-field transform on a closed box of node planes (3-D grids).

The DFT of the tangential fields on the six faces gives the equivalent surface currents ``J = n x H`` and
``M = -n x E``; their radiation integrals ``N = oint J exp(j k r_hat . r') dS'`` and ``L = oint M ...`` give the
far field (``exp(+j omega t)``, C. A. Balanis, *Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics*, 2nd ed., eqs. 6-122;
TH ch. 8)::

    r E_theta exp(j k r) = -j k / (4 pi) (L_phi + eta N_theta)
    r E_phi   exp(j k r) =  j k / (4 pi) (L_theta - eta N_phi)

``box = ((i0, i1), (j0, j1), (k0, k1))`` are the node indices of the faces; the box must enclose every source
and scatterer and lie in vacuum outside the PML. Create it before running; call :meth:`far_field` after.

methods.doc: ``(E_theta, E_phi)`` far-field patterns ``r E exp(j k r)`` (V), shape ``(n_freq, *theta.shape)``.

methods.name: radiated_power
methods.doc: ``(1 / (2 eta)) int (|E_theta|^2 + |E_phi|^2) dOmega`` of the far field, per frequency (W).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fem
children.doc:
2D magnetostatics in the z-component of the magnetic vector potential, P1 triangles.

Strong form, with ``B = curl(A_z e_z) = (dA/dy, -dA/dx)`` and the constitutive law ``H = nu(|B|^2) (B - Br)``::

    -div( nu grad A ) = J_z + (curl of nu Br)_z

Weak form solved here, for every test function ``v``::

    int nu grad A . grad v  =  int J v  +  int nu (Br_x dv/dy - Br_y dv/dx)

It is the stationarity condition of the energy functional (per metre of stack)::

    Pi(A) = sum_e area_e [ w_e(|B_e|^2) - nu_e Br_e . B_e ] - int J A

with ``w = nu |B|^2 / 2`` for linear media and ``w = int_0^|B| H db`` for nonlinear iron. ``Pi`` is convex
for monotone B-H curves, so Newton's method with a backtracking line search on ``Pi`` converges from
any start. ``-Pi`` at the solution equals the magnetic co-energy up to a term that does not depend on
the rotor angle; this is what :func:`pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.postprocess.torque_coenergy`
differentiates.

Boundary conditions: Dirichlet values on any node set, and periodic / anti-periodic node pairs
``A[slave] = sign * A[master]`` (eliminated through a sparse map ``A = P a + A_D``). Nodes with neither
are natural (zero tangential H, i.e. flux crosses the boundary at right angles).

Magnets are linear (``mu_r``, ``Br``); iron may be nonlinear. Materials are passed per element.

functions.name: solve_magnetostatic
functions.sig: (mesh: Mesh2D, nu: np.ndarray, J: np.ndarray | None = None, Br: np.ndarray | None = None, nonlinear: Sequence[tuple[np.ndarray, object]] = (), dirichlet: np.ndarray | None = None, dirichlet_values = None, periodic: Sequence[tuple[int, int, float]] | None = None, tol: float = 1e-09, max_iter: int = 60, A0: np.ndarray | None = None, geometry: Geometry | None = None, keep_tangent: bool = False) ->...
functions.doc:
Solve the A_z magnetostatic problem.

nu: (M,) reluctivity of linear elements (1/(mu0 mu_r)); for nonlinear elements it is ignored.
J: (M,) source current density (A/m^2); Br: (M, 2) remanence (T), zero outside magnets.
nonlinear: list of ``(element_mask, curve)`` with ``curve.nu``, ``curve.dnu``, ``curve.energy``.
dirichlet: node indices (default: ``mesh.boundary`` with A=0); pass an empty array for none.
Newton iterations stop when the reduced residual drops below ``tol`` times the load norm.

pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fem3d.cases
children.doc:
Closed-form 3-D cases on structured box meshes (no gmsh needed): used by the fast tests.

* :func:`manufactured_magnetostatic`: ``A = (0, 0, sin(pi x) sin(pi y))`` on the unit cube, ``J = curl curl A``.
* :func:`slab_eddy`: a conducting slab ``|z| < d`` in a uniform time-harmonic field ``B0 x`` parallel to it,
  ``B_x(z) = B0 cosh(k z) / cosh(k d)``, ``k = (1 + j) / delta``, ``delta = sqrt(2 / (omega mu0 sigma))``
  (e.g. Lammeraner and Stafl, *Eddy Currents*, Iliffe, 1966, ch. 2); with ``A* = y a(z)``,
  ``a = -B0 sinh(k z) / (k cosh(k d))`` inside and ``a = -B0 (z - d sgn z) - B0 tanh(k d) / k sgn z`` outside.
  Time-averaged loss per unit area of the slab (thickness ``2d``, both faces): ``B0^2 / (mu0^2 sigma delta)
  (sinh(2d/delta) - sin(2d/delta)) / (cosh(2d/delta) + cos(2d/delta))``, checked against the integral of
  ``sigma omega^2 |a|^2 / 2`` across the slab.

Edge-element solution of the slab with the exact ``n x A*`` on every boundary face; ``nz`` cells across

``B`` and the loss per unit area against the closed form.

children.doc:
GetDP as the external 3-D reference: the same gmsh meshes solved by GetDP's own edge-element formulations.

GetDP (https://getdp.info, GPL) is called as an executable (``apt install getdp``); no code of it is copied or
linked. Each problem file (``.pro``) is written here from the physical data only: GetDP's function spaces
(``BF_Edge``, Whitney 1-forms), its tree gauge (``EdgesOfTreeIn`` starting on the Dirichlet boundary), its
assembly, linear solver and post-processing integrals produce the numbers. Nothing of
:mod:`.nedelec` is used, so the agreement between the two measures implementation differences on identical
meshes.

children.doc:
Tetrahedral meshes for the 3-D edge-element solvers: topology (edges, faces, boundary), structured box meshes
and gmsh input.

A :class:`TetMesh` holds node coordinates, tetrahedra (four node indices each), a region tag per tetrahedron and
the names of the tags. Edges are oriented from the lower to the higher global node index; a tetrahedron's local
edge ``(a, b)`` carries the sign ``+1`` when ``tets[:, a] < tets[:, b]``, so the tangential continuity of the
Whitney (first-order Nedelec) functions holds across elements.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fem3d.nedelec
children.doc:
First-order Nedelec (Whitney edge) elements for 3-D magnetostatics and time-harmonic eddy currents.

Unknowns are the line integrals of the magnetic vector potential ``A`` along the mesh edges. On a tetrahedron the
edge function of edge ``(a, b)`` is ``W = lambda_a grad(lambda_b) - lambda_b grad(lambda_a)``, its curl the constant
``2 grad(lambda_a) x grad(lambda_b)``; ``B = curl A`` is therefore constant per tetrahedron and its normal
component is continuous across faces (``div B = 0`` exactly).

Magnetostatics: ``curl(nu curl A) = J + curl(nu Br)``, weakly

    sum_K int nu curl A . curl W = int J . W + int nu Br . curl W,

with ``n x A`` prescribed (Dirichlet edges, default zero: ``B . n = 0``) on the outer boundary. Nonlinear iron
by Newton on the energy functional, the tangent ``nu + 2 nu'(|B|^2) B B^T`` and a backtracking line search.

Eddy currents (modified vector potential ``A*``, ``E = -j omega A*`` in conductors, ``exp(+j omega t)``):
``curl(nu curl A) + j omega sigma A = J_s``.

Gauge: the curl-curl operator is singular on gradients. ``gauge="tree"`` removes the edges of a spanning tree of
the nodes that carry a gradient degree of freedom (nodes that are neither on a Dirichlet boundary nor in a
conductor), so the reduced matrix is non-singular and can be factorised. ``gauge="none"`` keeps every edge and
solves the consistent singular system with conjugate gradients (magnetostatics only). In both cases the source
vector is first made discretely divergence-free, ``G^T b = 0`` for the gradient ``G`` of every free node, by
subtracting its L2 projection on gradients (a P1 Poisson solve): a current density sampled on a mesh is not
discretely solenoidal, and a tree-gauged system turns its divergence into a spurious field.

References: A. Bossavit, *Computational Electromagnetism*, Academic Press, 1998 (Whitney forms, gauging by trees);
J.-M. Jin, *The Finite Element Method in Electromagnetics*, 3rd ed., Wiley, 2014 (edge elements);
R. Albanese and G. Rubinacci, "Solution of three dimensional eddy current problems by integral and differential
methods", IEEE Trans. Magn. 24 (1988) 98-101 (tree gauge and source consistency).

methods.doc: ``B = curl A`` per tetrahedron (M, 3).

methods.doc: The vector field ``A`` at points (NaN outside the mesh).

methods.doc:
``int J . A`` with the (discretely solenoidal) current load of the solve. For a source ``J = i j1``
it is ``i psi``, ``psi`` the flux linkage of the winding ``j1``, and ``d W' / d i = psi`` (co-energy
derivative tree: :mod:`pinneapple_physics.potential`, issue #928).

methods.name: J_at
methods.doc: Eddy current density phasor ``-j omega sigma A*`` at points (A/m^2, peak).

functions.name: tree_gauge
functions.sig: (mesh: TetMesh, fixed_edges: np.ndarray, root_nodes: np.ndarray, link_roots: bool = False) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Edges of a spanning tree that reaches every node not in ``root_nodes`` (breadth first from all roots at
once) using only edges not in ``fixed_edges``. Removing them leaves exactly one unknown per independent
curl: the gradient of every free node is spanned by tree edges.

``link_roots``: when the roots form several separate groups (a conductor's nodes and the outer boundary),
the gradient of a potential that is constant on each group (the conductor's floating potential) is zero
on every root edge and is not spanned by the forest, so the gauged system keeps that null space. With
``link_roots`` one more edge per extra group joins the groups into one tree.

functions.name: cocg
functions.sig: (A, b, M_inv, rtol: float = 1e-09, maxiter: int = 20000)
functions.doc:
Conjugate orthogonal conjugate gradients for complex symmetric ``A`` (van der Vorst and Melissen, IEEE
Trans. Magn. 26 (1990) 706-708): CG with the unconjugated product ``x^T y``, diagonal preconditioner
``M_inv`` (an array: diagonal) or symmetric preconditioner (a callable). Returns the solution and the number
of iterations; raises if the relative residual stays above ``rtol``.

functions.name: solve_magnetostatic
functions.sig: (mesh: TetMesh, nu, J = None, J_mask = None, Br = None, nonlinear: Mapping | None = None, dirichlet: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None, gauge: str = 'none', tol: float = 1e-09, max_iter: int = 50, space: EdgeSpace | None = None, a0: np.ndarray | None = None, cg_tol: float = 1e-10, verbose: bool = False) -> MagnetostaticSolution3D
functions.doc:
3-D magnetostatics on edge elements.

nu: reluctivity per tetrahedron (M,) or scalar (``1 / (mu0 mu_r)``); for nonlinear regions it is the initial
guess only. J: (M, 3) current density per tetrahedron or a callable of points (evaluated on ``J_mask``).
Br: (M, 3) remanence. nonlinear: ``{region_tag: curve}`` with ``curve.nu(s)``, ``curve.dnu(s)``,
``curve.energy(s)`` of ``s = |B|^2`` (e.g. :class:`~pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.materials.BHCurve`).
dirichlet: ``(edges, values)`` of prescribed edge circulations; default: every outer-boundary edge zero.
gauge: ``"none"`` (default: conjugate gradients with a Jacobi preconditioner on the singular, consistent
system) or ``"tree"`` (sparse LU of the tree-gauged system; exact but slow beyond ~1e5 unknowns).

functions.name: solve_eddy
functions.sig: (mesh: TetMesh, nu, sigma, omega: float, J, J_mask = None, dirichlet: tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray] | None = None, space: EdgeSpace | None = None, gauge: str = 'tree', rtol: float = 1e-09, solver: str = 'auto') -> EddySolution3D
functions.doc:
Time-harmonic eddy currents with the modified vector potential ``A*`` (linear media).

nu, sigma: per tetrahedron (or scalars); J: source current density phasor (M, 3) or callable, zero in the
conductors. The tree gauge spans the non-conducting nodes only (conductor nodes are roots), so ``A*`` is
unique in the conductors and carries the electric scalar potential there. ``gauge="tree"`` (default)
factorises the tree-gauged system (``solver``: see :func:`_complex_solver`) and refines the solution to
``rtol``;
``gauge="none"`` keeps every edge and solves with COCG and a Jacobi preconditioner, which is fast where it
converges but stalls and diverges on stiff cases (measured on TEAM problem 7: residual 2e-2 after 300
iterations, then growth), so it is opt-in.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fem3d.sphere
children.doc:
Permeable sphere in a uniform field: closed form, gmsh mesh, native edge-element and GetDP solutions.

A sphere of radius ``a`` and relative permeability ``mu_r`` in a uniform applied field ``B0`` (no currents) has

* inside, the uniform field ``B = 3 mu_r / (mu_r + 2) B0``;
* outside, the applied field plus a dipole of moment ``m = 4 pi a^3 (mu_r - 1) / (mu_r + 2) B0 / mu0``,
  with vector potential ``A = B0 x r / 2 + mu0 / (4 pi) m x r / |r|^3``

(Jackson, *Classical Electrodynamics*, 3rd ed., section 5.11; Griffiths, *Introduction to Electrodynamics*,
4th ed., example 6.1 for the analogous magnetized sphere). The computational domain is a ball of radius ``R``
with the exact exterior ``n x A`` on its surface, so the only error is discretisation (no truncation error).

classes.name: SphereCase
classes.doc:
Reference case of a magnetisable sphere (radius ``a``, relative permeability ``mu_r``) in a uniform field
``B0`` inside a ball of radius ``R``, with the exact field: uniform inside the sphere, a dipole's outside, and the
exact vector potential used on the outer boundary.

methods.name: A
methods.doc: Exact vector potential outside the sphere (used on the outer boundary).

functions.doc:
gmsh (OpenCASCADE) mesh of the sphere (physical volume 1, "sphere") inside the ball of radius ``R``
(volume 2, "air"), outer surface physical 3, element size ``h`` in the sphere growing to ``h_out`` (default
``2 h``) at the outer surface; written as ASCII msh 2.2.

functions.name: errors
functions.sig: (mesh: TetMesh, B: np.ndarray, case: SphereCase) -> dict
functions.doc:
Relative errors of a piecewise-constant ``B`` (M, 3): mean field in the sphere, L2 in the sphere and L2
over the whole domain (exact field sampled at a 4-point rule per tetrahedron).

functions.doc:
Outer-boundary edge values of ``A0 = B0 x r / 2`` (the truncated problem that GetDP solves in

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.fem3d.team7
children.doc:
TEAM workshop problem 7: asymmetrical conductor with a hole (linear eddy currents, 50 and 200 Hz).

Geometry, data and measured values from the TEAM problem 7 description (K. Fujiwara and T. Nakata, "Results for
benchmark problem 7 (asymmetrical conductor with a hole)", COMPEL 9 (3), 1990, 137-154; the problem description
with its tables of measured values is distributed with ElmerCSC's elmer-elmag repository as
``TEAM7/TEAM7_ProblemDescription.pdf``, and its ``TEAM7_A1B1.csv`` holds the 50 Hz, wt = 0 column of table 2a):

* aluminium plate 294 x 294 x 19 mm, sigma = 3.526e7 S/m, corner at the origin, with a 108 x 108 mm hole whose
  corner is at (18, 18) mm;
* a racetrack coil, 2742 ampere-turns, 25 mm wide and 100 mm high, from z = 49 to 149 mm (30 mm above the plate);
  inner square 150 mm with corner radius 25 mm, outer corner radius 50 mm; corner-arc centres at
  (144, 50), (244, 50), (244, 150), (144, 150) mm, so the coil spans x = 94..294 mm and y = 0..200 mm;
* the current is a maximum at wt = 0: ``i(t) = I0 cos(wt)``, phasor ``I0``; a field ``F`` at ``wt`` is
  ``Re(F exp(j wt))``, so ``wt = 90 deg`` gives ``-Im(F)``.

Measured quantities: ``Bz`` (gauss) along A1-B1 (y = 72, z = 34 mm) and A2-B2 (y = 144, z = 34 mm), x = 0..288 mm
every 18 mm; the eddy-current density ``Jy`` (1e6 A/m^2) along A3-B3 (y = 72, z = 19 mm) and A4-B4 (y = 72, z = 0)
at the 12 positions in :data:`X_J`. The benchmark states no tolerance band.

The coil current flows counter-clockwise seen from +z, which gives the positive ``Bz`` measured under the coil.

functions.name: coil_current_density
functions.sig: (points: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Uniform current density of the racetrack coil, counter-clockwise seen from +z (A/m^2), at points inside
the coil (direction tangent to the straight sides and to the corner arcs).

Returns
-------
J : np.ndarray [A/m2]
    Current density at ``points``.

functions.sig: (path, h_plate: float = 0.006, h_coil: float = 0.012, h_air: float = 0.08, margin: float = 0.3, h_layer: float | None = None) -> Path
functions.doc:
gmsh mesh: air box extending ``margin`` beyond the plate and coil (outer surface physical 9), the plate
(volume 1, "plate"), the coil (2, "coil"), air (3, "air"); sizes graded from the plate and coil.

functions.doc:
Probe points (m) of each measured line; points on the plate faces or the hole edges are moved 0.1 mm into
the aluminium (the eddy current is only defined there).

functions.name: solve
functions.sig: (msh, f: float, mesh: TetMesh | None = None, space: EdgeSpace | None = None, **kw)
functions.doc: Native A* solution of TEAM 7 at frequency ``f`` on the gmsh file ``msh``.

functions.name: probe
functions.sig: (sol) -> dict
functions.doc:
Computed values on the measured lines, in the units of :data:`MEASURED`: ``{(line, wt): values}`` for wt
= 0 and 90 deg. ``Bz`` is averaged over the tetrahedra around each probe point (it is constant per
tetrahedron); the eddy current is the A* field at the point.

functions.name: compare
functions.sig: (computed: dict, f: int) -> dict
functions.doc:
Differences against the measured values per line and instant: rms, max and the rms relative to the
largest measured magnitude on the line. For the eddy-current lines, also the rms relative to the table of the
other face of the plate (``rms_rel_peak_other_face``): the computed current is larger on the face nearer the
coil (z = 19 mm), as the skin depth (12 mm at 50 Hz, 6 mm at 200 Hz) requires, while the table puts the
larger values on A4-B4 (z = 0); both pairings are reported.

functions.sig: (msh, freqs = (50, 200), **kw) -> dict
functions.doc: Solve and compare at each frequency; sizes and times included.

children.doc:
3-D finite elements for electromagnetics: first-order Nedelec (Whitney edge) elements on tetrahedra.

* :mod:`.mesh` -- :class:`TetMesh` (edges, faces, boundary, point location), structured box meshes, gmsh input.
* :mod:`.nedelec` -- :class:`EdgeSpace` (element matrices, sources, evaluation), nonlinear magnetostatics by Newton
  (:func:`solve_magnetostatic`), time-harmonic eddy currents with the modified vector potential
  (:func:`solve_eddy`), tree gauge, discretely solenoidal sources, energy and co-energy.
* :mod:`.sphere` -- permeable sphere in a uniform field (closed form, gmsh mesh, errors).
* :mod:`.cases` -- closed-form cases on box meshes: manufactured magnetostatics, conducting slab (skin effect).
* :mod:`.getdp3d` -- GetDP as the external reference on the same meshes.
children.summary: 3-D finite elements for electromagnetics: first-order Nedelec (Whitney edge) elements on tetrahedra.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.hysteresis
children.doc:
Nonlinear magnetisation: the Froehlich-Kennelly saturation curve and the Jiles-Atherton hysteresis model.

:class:`FrohlichKennelly` is single-valued: ``B = mu0 H + H / (alpha + beta |H|)`` (Froehlich 1881, Kennelly
1891; the polarisation saturates at ``1/beta``, the initial relative permeability is
``1 + 1 / (mu0 alpha)``). It exposes the interface of :class:`.materials.BHCurve` (``h``, ``nu``, ``dnu``,
``energy`` as functions of ``s = |B|^2``) with every quantity in closed form, so it plugs straight into the
Newton solver of :mod:`.fem`.

:class:`JilesAtherton` is the hysteresis model of D. C. Jiles and D. L. Atherton, *Theory of ferromagnetic
hysteresis*, J. Magn. Magn. Mater. 61 (1986) 48-60. With the effective field ``He = H + alpha M``, the
anhysteretic ``Man = Ms L(He / a)`` (``L(x) = coth x - 1/x``), the split ``M = Mrev + Mirr``,
``Mrev = c (Man - Mirr)`` and the pinning law ``dMirr/dHe = delta_M (Man - Mirr) / (delta k)``
(``delta = sign(dH/dt)``; ``delta_M = 1`` when ``delta (Man - M) > 0``, else 0, which keeps the irreversible
susceptibility non-negative), the chain rule gives, with ``u = delta_M (Man - M) / (delta k)`` and
``g = dMan/dHe``::

    dM/dH = (u + c g) / (1 - alpha (u + c g))

This is derived from the definitions above rather than taken from a later paper, several of which use
inequivalent rearrangements. It is integrated along an applied ``H(t)`` path with classical RK4 on each
monotone segment; the step error is measured in the tests. ``loss_per_cycle`` is ``oint H dB``.

classes.name: FrohlichKennelly
classes.doc: ``B = mu0 H + H / (alpha + beta H)`` for ``H >= 0`` (odd extension). ``alpha`` in m/H, ``beta`` in 1/T.

methods.name: from_saturation
methods.doc: Initial relative permeability and saturation polarisation ``Js`` (T).

methods.name: h
methods.doc:
Inverse of :meth:`b` for ``b >= 0`` (positive root of ``mu0 beta H^2 + (mu0 alpha + 1 - beta b) H
- alpha b = 0``), written in the cancellation-free form ``2 c / (-q - sqrt(q^2 - 4 a c))``.

methods.name: dnu
methods.doc:
d nu / d s, ``s = |B|^2``: ``(H'(b) b - H(b)) / (2 b^3)``, evaluated at ``b >= 1e-6`` T (the limit at
``b -> 0`` is finite).

methods.name: energy
methods.doc: ``w(b) = int_0^b H db' = b H(b) - int_0^H(b) B dh`` (Legendre), closed form.

methods.name: loss_per_cycle
methods.doc: ``oint H dB`` (J/m^3) over the samples from ``start`` (the caller passes a closed cycle).

methods.name: coercivity
methods.doc: |H| where B crosses zero on the descending branch (linear interpolation).

methods.name: remanence
methods.doc: B where H crosses zero on the descending branch (T).

classes.name: JilesAtherton
classes.doc:
Jiles-Atherton parameters: saturation magnetisation ``Ms`` (A/m), anhysteretic shape ``a`` (A/m),
pinning ``k`` (A/m), reversibility ``c`` (0..1), inter-domain coupling ``alpha``.

methods.sig: (H: float, M: float, delta: float) -> float

methods.name: trace
methods.doc:
Integrate ``M`` along the applied field samples ``H_path`` (RK4 with ``substeps`` steps between
samples; the direction ``delta`` is that of each segment).

methods.sig: (H_max: float, n: int = 400, cycles: int = 2) -> tuple[HysteresisLoop, int]
methods.doc:
Initial curve then ``cycles`` full cycles ``+H_max -> -H_max -> +H_max``; returns the loop and the
index where the last cycle starts.

functions.doc: ``L(x) = coth x - 1/x`` with its series ``x/3 - x^3/45`` near 0.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machine
children.doc:
Radial-flux machine with surface permanent magnets (or none: a reluctance rotor), 2D A_z FEM.

The cross-section is meshed with :func:`~pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.mesh.polar_mesh`:
rotor rings turn with the rotor and a one-layer moving band in the middle of the air gap is
re-triangulated for each rotor angle, so rotor and stator elements keep their indices and shapes at
every angle (smooth co-energy, rotor-frame quantities for losses, a fixed design-variable set for
topology optimization). Slots, teeth and magnets are resolved on the polar grid (their edges snap to
the nearest grid line); ``n_theta`` sets the angular resolution.

    from pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machine import SPMMachine
    m = SPMMachine()                                   # 4 poles, 24 slots, illustrative data
    sol = m.solve(theta=0.0, currents=(0.0, 0.0, 0.0))  # no load
    T = m.torque(sol)                                  # Maxwell stress (Arkkio), N m
    Tc = m.torque_coenergy(0.01, (0.0, 0.0, 0.0))      # virtual work, N m
    psi = m.flux_linkage(sol)                          # Wb-turn per phase

Conventions: angles in radians, rotor angle ``theta`` counter-clockwise, torque on the rotor positive
counter-clockwise; ``currents`` are the instantaneous phase currents (A). Phase ``k`` of a balanced
supply is ``I cos(p theta + phi0 + pi/2 + gamma - 2 pi k / 3)``, where ``phi0`` is the electrical angle
of the magnet flux linkage at ``theta = 0`` (from :meth:`SPMMachine.pm_flux_angle`), so ``gamma = 0`` puts
the current on the q-axis (in phase with the back-EMF) and ``gamma > 0`` advances it towards -d.

Default dimensions and materials are illustrative (not a commercial design); the iron curve is
:func:`~pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.materials.illustrative_steel`.

classes.name: ScaledCurve
classes.sig: (curve, w: np.ndarray)
classes.doc:
Density-interpolated reluctivity ``nu = nu0 + w (nu_iron(s) - nu0)`` with per-element weights ``w``
(topology optimization of iron). ``curve`` is a B-H curve object or a linear ``mu_r``.

Air annuli used by the Maxwell-stress torque: the gap layers on the rotor side and on the

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines
pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.design
children.doc:
Rotor design of the V-magnet IPM machine with the design-study core of :mod:`pinneapple_design.design_optimizer`:
the FEA as a reference evaluator, a Gaussian-process surrogate with active learning, NSGA-II, re-verification of
every Pareto design by FEA, and the FEA calls this saves against a GA that calls the FEA directly.

* :func:`rotor_evaluator` (an ``IPMRotorEvaluator``) -- design vector (magnet width ``W4``, thickness ``H3``, V depth ``H0``, opening ``W0``,
  bridge ``H1`` of :class:`~.geometry.VRotor`) to mean torque and torque ripple at a fixed current (FEA) and magnet
  mass (exact). Designs whose polygons cross or leave the pole (:func:`~.geometry.geometry_errors`) are returned as
  invalid, without a solve.
* :func:`rotor_design_problem` -- maximise torque, minimise magnet mass, ripple below a limit.
* :func:`hybrid_vs_fea_only` -- surrogate-assisted NSGA-II (LHS start, rounds of GP fit, NSGA-II on the GP, FEA on
  points along its front) against NSGA-II on the FEA itself; the hypervolume of the FEA-verified front of each,
  and how many FEA calls the FEA-only GA needs to reach the hybrid's hypervolume.

functions.name: rotor_evaluator
functions.sig: (**kwargs)
functions.doc:
An :class:`IPMRotorEvaluator` (keyword arguments of its constructor). The class is built on first use: the
design core it subclasses imports torch.

functions.name: rotor_design_problem
functions.sig: (evaluator = None, ripple_max: float = 0.3)
functions.doc: Maximise ``torque``, minimise ``magnet_mass``, subject to ``ripple <= ripple_max``.

functions.name: hybrid_vs_fea_only
functions.sig: (problem, *, n_initial: int = 24, rounds: int = 3, n_verify: int = 8, ga_budget: int = 400, surrogate_budget: int = 1500, seed: int = 0, verifier = None, progress = None) -> dict
functions.doc:
Run both studies on ``problem`` (its evaluator is the FEA) and compare them at equal quality.

Quality is the hypervolume of the feasible FEA-evaluated designs, objectives normalised by the ideal and nadir
points of all FEA data of both runs. Returns the hybrid's FEA calls, the FEA-only GA's hypervolume history, the
number of FEA calls at which it first reaches the hybrid's hypervolume (None if not within ``ga_budget``), and
with ``verifier`` (a finer FEA evaluator) the re-evaluation of every design of the hybrid front.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.drive
children.doc:
Drive model of a synchronous machine: dq steady state, MTPA and flux weakening under inverter limits,
efficiency map and drive-cycle energy.

The machine enters as a *flux map*, any object with ``psi(i_d, i_q) -> (psi_d, psi_q)``, ``torque(i_d, i_q)`` and
``core_loss(i_d, i_q, f_e)`` (vectorised over arrays):

* :class:`LinearDQ` -- constant ``L_d``, ``L_q``, ``psi_m``: ``T = 1.5 p (psi_m i_q + (L_d - L_q) i_d i_q)``; its MTPA,
  base speed and flux-weakening torque have closed forms (:meth:`LinearDQ.mtpa_closed_form`,
  :meth:`LinearDQ.max_torque_closed_form`) that verify the numerical optimiser.
* :class:`FluxMap` -- tables of the FEA (:meth:`FluxMap.from_fea` on an :class:`~.pmsm.IPMMachine`): mean torque and dq
  flux linkages on an ``(i_d, i_q)`` grid (saturation and cross-saturation included), and per grid point the
  frequency-free iron-loss sums and the magnet-loss coefficient (:meth:`~.pmsm.IPMMachine.loss_components`), so the
  core loss at any speed is ``k_h f^alpha S_h + k_c f^2 S_c + k_e f^1.5 S_e + c_m f^2``.

Steady state (amplitude-invariant dq, peak values): ``v_d = R i_d - w_e psi_q``, ``v_q = R i_q + w_e psi_d``, phase
current amplitude ``|i| <= I_max``, phase voltage amplitude ``|v| <= V_max`` (``V_dc / sqrt 3`` for space-vector PWM
in its linear range, :func:`v_max_svpwm`). :class:`Drive` picks for a requested torque and speed the feasible current
of least total loss (copper ``1.5 R |i|^2`` plus core loss); without the voltage limit this is the
maximum-torque-per-ampere point when core loss is ignored, and at high speed it is the flux-weakening point.

:class:`Vehicle` turns a speed trace into wheel torque and speed (road load ``m g C_rr + 0.5 rho C_d A v^2``,
inertia, single gear with efficiency); :func:`cycle_energy` integrates the battery-side energy of a drive over it,
with regeneration up to the drive's torque envelope. :func:`wltc_class3b` loads the WLTC class 3b speed trace
(UN GTR No. 15, Annex 1).

classes.doc: Machine with constant inductances: ``psi_d = psi_m + L_d i_d``, ``psi_q = L_q i_q``.

methods.name: mtpa_closed_form
methods.doc: MTPA currents at amplitude ``current``: ``i_d = (psi_m - sqrt(psi_m^2 + 8 (L_q - L_d)^2 I^2)) / (4 (L_q - L_d))``.

Largest torque at electrical speed ``w_e`` with ``R = 0`` (current circle and voltage ellipse):
the MTPA point below base speed, the circle-ellipse intersection above it (valid up to the
maximum-torque-per-volt region, i.e. while ``psi_m > L_d I_max``).

machine's symmetry extends the maps to negative ``i_q`` (``psi_d`` even, ``psi_q`` and torque odd).

methods.sig: (machine, I_max: float, n_d: int = 9, n_q: int = 9, n_positions: int = 6, loss_n: int = 5, loss_steps: int = 24, loss_fit = None, progress = None) -> FluxMap
methods.doc:
Sample ``machine`` (an :class:`~.pmsm.IPMMachine`) on ``i_d in [-I_max, 0]``, ``i_q in [0, I_max]``:
torque and flux on an ``n_d x n_q`` grid (``n_positions`` rotor angles each), loss data on a coarser
``loss_n x loss_n`` grid (``loss_steps`` angles over an electrical period each). ``loss_fit``: a
:class:`~.steel.LossFit` (default: :func:`~.steel.fit_iron_loss` of the machine's steel up to 1 kHz).

classes.name: Drive
classes.doc:
A machine (flux map) fed by a voltage-source inverter: current and voltage amplitude limits, phase
resistance, end-winding leakage inductance ``L_end`` (:mod:`.endwinding`). ``n_d`` sets the resolution of the search
over ``i_d`` (refined by golden section).

methods.name: operating_point
methods.sig: (T_req: float, speed: float, include_core_loss: bool = True) -> dict | None
methods.doc:
Least-loss feasible currents for torque ``T_req`` (N m) at mechanical speed ``speed`` (rad/s), or None.
Returns currents, voltage amplitude, losses and efficiency (motoring ``P/(P+L)``, generating ``(|P|-L)/|P|``).

methods.name: max_torque
methods.sig: (speed: float, n: int = 361, generating: bool = False) -> dict
methods.doc:
Largest feasible torque (or braking torque) at mechanical speed ``speed``. Along any ray of current
angle ``gamma`` in [0, 90 deg] towards -d the torque grows with the amplitude, so the maximum lies on the
outer boundary of the feasible set (current circle or voltage ellipse, which covers the
maximum-torque-per-volt region): a scan over ``n`` angles, refined by repeated zooming.

methods.name: efficiency_map
methods.doc:
Efficiency and loss (NaN where infeasible) on ``speeds`` (rad/s) x ``torques``, and the motoring and braking
envelopes. ``torques`` in N m (negative = generating), or with ``relative=True`` as fractions in [-1, 1] of the
motoring (> 0) and braking (< 0) envelope at each speed, so the map reaches the envelope everywhere; the
torque values used are returned as a (speeds, torques) array ``T``.

classes.name: Vehicle
classes.doc:
Longitudinal vehicle: test mass (kg), rolling resistance, drag area C_d A (m^2), wheel radius (m), single gear
ratio and its efficiency, rotating-mass factor (equivalent inertia as a fraction of the mass).

methods.name: motor_demand
methods.doc: Motor speed (rad/s) and torque (N m) at the mid-points of the trace (central acceleration).

functions.name: v_max_svpwm
functions.sig: (v_dc: float) -> float
functions.doc: Largest phase-voltage amplitude of space-vector PWM in its linear range: ``V_dc / sqrt(3)``.

functions.name: copper_resistance
functions.sig: (series_turns: float, conductor_area: float, stack_length: float, end_length: float, temperature: float = 20.0, rho20: float = 1.724e-08, alpha: float = ALPHA_CU, parallel_paths: int = 1) -> float
functions.doc:
DC phase resistance: ``rho(T) N 2 (L + l_end) / (A a^2)`` with ``N`` series turns per phase, ``A`` the copper
area of one conductor, ``l_end`` the end-turn length per side, ``a`` parallel paths (IEC 60028 standard copper
``1.724e-8 Ohm m`` at 20 degC by default).

functions.name: prius_phase_resistance
functions.sig: (temperature: float = 100.0) -> tuple[float, dict]
functions.doc:
Phase resistance of the 2004 Prius motor from the winding data of pyleecan's ``Toyota_Prius.json``: 72 series
turns, 13 strands of 0.912 mm per conductor, 83.82 mm stack. The end-turn length per side is an estimate: a
half circle over the coil pitch (6 slots at the mid-slot radius) plus twice the axial overhang (19.4 mm).

Returns
-------
R : float [ohm]
    Phase resistance at ``temperature`` (degC).
info : dict
    The winding data used, each key with its unit in the name.

functions.name: wltc_class3b
functions.sig: () -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]
functions.doc:
WLTC class 3b: time (s) and vehicle speed (m/s), 1 Hz, 0..1800 s (UN GTR No. 15, Annex 1).

Returns
-------
t : np.ndarray [s]
    Time.
v : np.ndarray [m/s]
    Vehicle speed.

functions.name: cycle_energy
functions.sig: (drive: Drive, vehicle: Vehicle, t: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray, envelope_speeds: int = 25) -> dict
functions.doc:
Battery-side energy of ``drive`` over the speed trace (``t`` s, ``v`` m/s): motoring ``P_mech + losses``,
regeneration ``P_mech - losses`` (negative) up to the braking-torque envelope, the rest by friction brakes.
Operating points come from a table of :meth:`Drive.operating_point` on a speed x torque grid, interpolated
bilinearly in loss (tabulating keeps the cycle to a few hundred optimisations).

children.summary: Drive model of a synchronous machine: dq steady state, MTPA and flux weakening under inverter limits, efficiency map and drive-cycle energy.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.endwinding
children.doc:
End windings: resistance and leakage inductance of the coil ends, outside the 2-D cross-section.

Each coil end is a thin conductor on the cylinder at the mean slot radius ``r_c``: axially out of the stack by the
overhang ``e``, then a half circle (in the developed cylinder surface) over the coil span, then back. Its length per
coil side, ``e + pi s / 4`` with ``s`` the developed coil span (half of ``2 e + pi s / 2`` per coil end), is the
end-turn length used by :func:`~.drive.prius_phase_resistance`, so resistance and inductance share one geometry.

:func:`end_winding_inductance` integrates the phase inductances of these conductors (Neumann's formula with the
thin-wire kernel, :func:`~..statics.filament_inductance`), both ends, with the coil bundle as a round conductor of
the slot's copper area, in air and with the stator end face as an infinitely permeable mirror; the two bound the
real laminated end face. The dq leakage inductance of a balanced three-phase winding is ``L_aa - M_ab``; it adds to
L_d and L_q (``Drive(..., L_end=...)``).

functions.name: coil_end_path
functions.sig: (r_c: float, phi_a: float, phi_b: float, overhang: float, n_arc: int = 48) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc: Polyline (n, 3) of one coil end from the stack face at angle ``phi_a`` to ``phi_b`` (z >= 0 outside).

functions.name: end_winding_paths
functions.sig: (layout: list, slots: int, coil_pitch: int, r_c: float, overhang: float) -> list[tuple[int, np.ndarray]]
functions.doc:
(phase, path) of every coil end of a single-layer winding: each slot with a positive coil side is joined to the
slot ``coil_pitch`` further on, which must carry the same phase with the opposite sign.

functions.name: end_winding_inductance
functions.sig: (geometry, layout: list, turns_per_coil: float, coil_pitch: int, overhang: float, pieces_per_metre: float = 300.0) -> dict
functions.doc:
Phase self and mutual inductances of both coil ends (H), and the dq end leakage ``L_aa - M_ab``, in air and
with the end face as an iron mirror.

children.summary: End windings: resistance and leakage inductance of the coil ends, outside the 2-D cross-section.

Write an unstructured grid; ``points`` (N, 2 or 3), ``cells`` (M, 3) triangles or (M, 6) wedges; data arrays
of shape (M,) / (M, c) and (N,) / (N, c).

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.geometry
children.doc:
Parametric cross-sections of radial-flux machines: V-shaped interior magnets and round-bottom slots.

A machine is described per *sector*: one rotor pole and one stator slot pitch, each a list of named closed
polygons inside an annular sector (straight edges; arcs are discretised by :func:`arc`). The mesher
(:mod:`.mesher`) meshes one sector with every polygon edge as a mesh edge and copies it around the circle,
so the regions of the mesh are the polygons exactly, and every pole and every slot has the same mesh.

Parametrisations (lengths in metres, angles in radians):

* :class:`VRotor` -- a lamination with one V of two rectangular magnets per pole, the parametrisation of
  pyleecan's ``HoleM50`` (Apache-2.0; P. Bonneel, E. Devillers et al.): opening ``W0`` and depth ``H0`` of the
  V, tangential-bridge thickness ``H1``, magnet thickness ``H3`` and width ``W4``, inter-pole rib ``W3``,
  centre-post width ``W1``. The V angle follows from them (:attr:`VRotor.v_angle`).
* :class:`RoundBottomSlots` -- open trapezoidal slots with a round bottom (pyleecan ``SlotW11``): opening
  ``W0`` x ``H0``, wedge ``H1``, body width ``W1`` at the top and ``W2`` at the bottom, depth ``H2``,
  bottom fillet radius ``R1``.

:func:`prius_2004` returns the 2004 Toyota Prius traction motor with the dimensions of pyleecan's
``Toyota_Prius.json`` (48 slots, 8 poles, 83.82 mm stack).

classes.name: Polygon
classes.doc:
A named closed polygon (vertices counter-clockwise or clockwise, last vertex not repeated).

``magnetization``: for magnets, the angle (in the sector frame) of the remanence of a north pole.

classes.name: SectorGeometry
classes.doc:
Annular sector ``r_in < r < r_out``, ``-span/2 < phi < span/2``, holding polygons (later ones win where
they overlap) in a background region ``fill``. ``arc_nodes_in``/``arc_nodes_out``: extra angles that must
be nodes on the inner/outer arc (corners of polygons that touch the arcs).

classes.name: VRotor
classes.doc: Interior-PM rotor with one V of two magnets per pole (pyleecan ``HoleM50`` parametrisation).

methods.name: v_angle
methods.doc: Opening angle of the V between the two magnets (radians; pi is a flat, tangential magnet).

methods.name: sector
methods.doc: One pole centred on +x: pockets (air) and magnets, magnetised normal to their wide face, outwards.

classes.name: RoundBottomSlots
classes.doc: Stator lamination with open slots: opening, straight-sided body, semicircular or filleted bottom.

methods.name: sector
methods.doc:
One slot pitch centred on the slot axis (+x): regions ``slot`` (winding), ``opening`` and ``wedge``
(air), in the background ``stator_iron``.

methods.name: slot_area
methods.doc: Exact area of the winding region: trapezoid plus the rounded bottom.

classes.name: MachineGeometry
classes.doc: Rotor + stator + air gap. ``gap_layers`` rings split the gap (moving band in the middle).

functions.name: polygon_area
functions.sig: (xy: np.ndarray) -> float
functions.doc: Signed area of a closed polygon (counter-clockwise positive).

functions.name: arc
functions.sig: (center: complex, radius: float, a0: float, a1: float, h: float, even: bool = False) -> np.ndarray
functions.doc:
Points of a circular arc from angle ``a0`` to ``a1`` (both included), spacing at most ``h``; ``even``: an even
number of intervals, so the mid-angle is a vertex (arcs symmetric about a mirror axis).

functions.name: prius_2004
functions.sig: () -> MachineGeometry
functions.doc:
2004 Toyota Prius traction motor: dimensions of pyleecan's ``Toyota_Prius.json`` (pyleecan 1.4.2,
Apache-2.0), which models the machine of the ORNL evaluation reports (ORNL/TM-2004/185, ORNL/TM-2006/423).

functions.name: geometry_errors
functions.sig: (sector: SectorGeometry, tol: float = 1e-09) -> list[str]
functions.doc:
Reasons why a sector is not a valid cross-section (empty when valid): polygons that self-intersect, cross each
other, overlap (a vertex strictly inside another polygon), or leave the annular sector.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.getdp
children.doc:
Independent cross-check of the machine FEA with gmsh (mesh) and GetDP (solver).

gmsh (https://gmsh.info) and GetDP (https://getdp.info) are GPL programs used here as external executables only
(``gmsh`` and ``getdp`` on the path; no code of theirs is copied or linked). For one rotor angle and one set of
phase currents, :func:`solve` writes

* a gmsh geometry (``.geo``, built-in kernel) of the full cross-section from the same polygons as the mesher of
  :mod:`.mesher` (:func:`write_geo`): every region is a plane surface bounded by shared lines, iron regions with
  the pole and slot holes as inner loops; the rotor is turned by ``theta``, so each angle has its own unstructured
  mesh (no moving band);
* a GetDP problem (``.pro``, :func:`write_pro`): A_z magnetostatics in ``H(curl)`` with perpendicular edge
  (nodal) functions, nonlinear iron from the B-H table (Akima interpolation of ``nu(b^2)``, Newton-Raphson with the
  ``JacNL`` tangent term), linear magnets with remanence, coil current densities, ``A = 0`` on the shaft and outer
  circles; post-processing in GetDP of the Arkkio torque over the air gap and of the three phase flux linkages,

runs both programs and returns their numbers. Nothing of this package's own mesher, solver or post-processing is
used for the result, so the agreement with :class:`~.pmsm.IPMMachine` measures discretisation and implementation
differences between two independent codes on identical geometry and material data.

functions.name: available
functions.sig: () -> bool

functions.name: write_geo
functions.sig: (path, geometry: MachineGeometry, theta: float = 0.0, n_gap: int = 960, h_max: float | None = None, grading: float = 0.2, h: float = 0.001) -> dict
functions.doc:
gmsh geometry of the full machine at rotor angle ``theta``. Returns the physical-region numbers, the polygon
areas of the slots and the magnetisation angles of the magnets (global frame).

functions.name: write_pro
functions.sig: (path, geometry: MachineGeometry, info: dict, steel, Br: float, mu_r: float, layout: list, turns_per_slot: float, currents, parallel_paths: int = 1) -> None
functions.doc: GetDP problem for the regions of :func:`write_geo`.

functions.name: solve
functions.sig: (geometry: MachineGeometry, theta: float, currents, steel, Br: float, mu_r: float, layout: list, turns_per_slot: float, n_gap: int = 960, workdir = None, keep: bool = False, timeout: float = 600.0) -> dict
functions.doc: Mesh with gmsh and solve with GetDP; returns torque (N m), phase flux linkages (Wb), element count, times.

functions.name: write_geo_3d
functions.sig: (path, geometry: MachineGeometry, n_gap: int, layers_stack: int, end_air: float, layers_air: int) -> dict
functions.doc:
The cross-section of :func:`write_geo` (rotor at angle 0) extruded over half the stack (``z`` from the
mid-stack plane to the end face) into prisms, plus an air extension of length ``end_air`` beyond the end face
(``end_air = 0``: none).

functions.name: write_pro_3d
functions.sig: (path, info: dict, steel, Br: float, mu_r: float, stacking_factor: float, pole_half_angle: float, r_gap: tuple[float, float], with_end_air: bool) -> None
functions.doc:
GetDP problem: magnetic scalar potential ``H = -grad(phi)``, ``div(mu H + Br) = 0``, nonlinear iron by Picard
iteration on the secant permeability (Newton on ``mu(h)`` diverges for this formulation),
natural boundaries (no flux through the shaft, outer and mid-stack surfaces), ``phi`` fixed at one node. Output:
the radial air-gap flux under pole 0 (volume integral of ``B_r`` over the gap divided by its radial thickness).

functions.name: end_leakage_3d
functions.sig: (geometry: MachineGeometry, steel, Br: float, mu_r: float, n_gap: int = 240, layers_stack: int = 6, end_air: float = 0.04, layers_air: int = 6, workdir = None, timeout: float = 3600.0) -> dict
functions.doc:
No-load air-gap flux under a pole of the 3-D half stack with an air region beyond the end face, divided by the
same model without it (identical mesh in the stack: the 2-D field extruded). Returns both fluxes, the ratio, and
the element counts and times.

children.name: pinneapple_simulation.electromagnetics.machines.interop
children.doc:
Interoperability of the machine models: pyleecan, FEMM, MATLAB, DXF and the PINNeAPPle data contracts.

* pyleecan (Apache-2.0, https://github.com/Eomys/pyleecan): :func:`from_pyleecan` reads a machine file
  (``MachineIPMSM`` with a ``HoleM50`` rotor and a ``SlotW11`` stator, e.g. ``Toyota_Prius.json``) into a
  :class:`~.geometry.MachineGeometry` and its winding; :func:`to_pyleecan` writes the parameters back in pyleecan's
  field names (the parametrisations are the same, so the round trip is exact).
* FEMM (https://www.femm.info): :func:`femm_lua` writes a Lua script for FEMM's magnetics module that draws the full
  cross-section (every polygon of the mesher's sector geometry, copied around the circle), assigns the B-H curve,
  magnets (direction per piece), coils (circuits per phase and turns) and runs the analysis. FEMM is not available
  where this package is tested; the script is checked by re-reading its own nodes and segments
  (:func:`read_femm_lua_polygons`).
* MATLAB: :func:`to_mat` / :func:`from_mat` (``scipy.io``) for flux maps, efficiency maps and field solutions.
* DXF: :func:`to_dxf` writes the cross-section as closed polylines on one layer per region (DXF R12, ASCII);
  :func:`read_dxf_polylines` reads such files back.
* ElmerFEM: :func:`elmer_case` writes the gmsh geometry and a MagnetoDynamics2D solver input file (``.sif``)
  (not run here: ElmerFEM was not available).
* gmsh / GetDP: :mod:`.getdp` writes, meshes and solves the machine (used as the independent cross-check).
* Contracts: :func:`rotor_parameter_space` (``ParameterSpace`` of the rotor design variables) and
  :func:`fluxmap_dataset` (a flux map as a table with a ``DatasetSpec``, written by
  :func:`pinneapple_data.contracts.tables.write_table` to CSV, Parquet or HDF5).

functions.doc:
Every polygon of the full cross-section as ``(region, xy, magnetisation angle)``: pole ``k`` turned by
``k * pole pitch`` (magnetisation reversed on odd poles), slot ``k`` by ``k * slot pitch``.

functions.sig: (geometry: MachineGeometry, steel, magnet, layout: list, turns_per_slot: float, currents = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), magnet_temperature: float = 20.0, filename: str = 'machine.fem', h: float = 0.001) -> str

Lua script for FEMM 4.2 (magnetics, planar, millimetres) of the full machine at the rotor angle of the
mesher's sector geometry (pole 0 on +x). ``layout``: (phase, sign) per slot; ``currents``: phase currents (A).

Cross-section as closed POLYLINE entities (DXF R12, ASCII, millimetres by default), one layer per region kind

A flux map (attributes ``i_d``, ``i_q`` grids and ``psi_d``, ``psi_q``, ``T`` tables, e.g. a drive ``FluxMap``)

functions.sig: (directory, geometry: MachineGeometry, steel, magnet, layout: list, turns_per_slot: float, currents = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0), theta: float = 0.0, magnet_temperature: float = 20.0, n_gap: int = 960) -> dict

An ElmerFEM case (MagnetoDynamics2D, steady) of the machine at rotor angle ``theta``: ``machine.geo`` (gmsh,

and convert with ``ElmerGrid 14 2 machine.msh -autoclean``; body numbers in the SIF are the gmsh physical surface
numbers in order. Written to the documented SIF keywords; ElmerFEM was not available where this was tested, so
the case itself has not been run.
